findings.problem: New York and Oregon have no row, and the design says 'A State with no row follows the federal rate', so NY and OR employees get USD 7.25. The research carries regional rates: NY 17.00 (NYC, Long Island, Westchester) / 16.00 (rest of State) from 2026-01-01 [US-NYS5-002]; OR standard 15.05 -> 15.55, Portland metro 16.30 -> 16.80, nonurban 14.05 -> 14.55, changing 2026-07-01 [US-ORS5-002]. Those keys are ny.labour.minwage.* and or.labour.minwage.*, which the <st>.minwage.hourly selector missed.
findings.expected: Add NY and OR rows bound to ny.labour.minwage.{nyc_li_westchester,rest_of_state}.hourly and or.labour.minwage.{standard,portland_metro,nonurban}.hourly, with the region taken from DD 'County of primary employment' / 'Work location' at the work date. The fallback sentence applies only to States with no State minimum wage (AL, LA, MS, SC, TN) or one at or below the federal rate (GA, NC, NH, OK).

findings.problem: wa.wc.supplemental_pension.rate = 0.1912 USD per hour (L&I 2026 rates are per worker-hour, US-WAS5-019) is labelled method 'rate on wages', so the engine would take 19.12% of wages.
findings.expected: Method 'per hour' (rate_per_hour x hours worked), like wa.wc.class101.employee_hourly.

findings.problem: Flag 58414 forces the aggregate method for an exempt employee (58403 = 1), but 58524 = MAX(0; FIT_SCHEDULE(58501 + below) - 58507) has no 58403 gate. 58507 is 0 for that employee, so the formula withholds full schedule tax on a bonus. The prose says the aggregate method gives no withholding, but the formula does not do that.
findings.expected: 58524 = IF(EQUALS($58403;1); 0; IF(EQUALS($58406;1); 0; IF(EQUALS($58409;1); 0; IF(EQUALS($58414;2); MAX(0; FIT_SCHEDULE(58501 + below) - 58507); 0)))). 58509 stays ungated by 58403.

findings.problem: The threshold tests zero the tax below the threshold and then tax only the current period. When the household (3,000), election-worker (2,500) or agricultural (150 / 2,500) threshold is crossed, all cash wages of the year become FICA wages, but the earlier wages are never caught up. The FUTA test is per quarter ('household_wages_quarter < 1,000'), whereas the rule is 1,000 in any calendar quarter of the current or preceding year, and then all FUTA wages up to 7,000 for the year.
findings.expected: Crossing period: base = YTD wages including the current period (catch-up), capped by the wage base. FUTA liability = any quarter of the current or preceding year >= the threshold (household 1,000; agricultural 20,000), then normal FUTA on the year's wages to 7,000 with catch-up.

findings.problem: 58428 (date earned) is applied to every programme row on the strength of the Massachusetts source alone ('the other rows carry the same rule until a State annex says otherwise'). No register row supports 'earned' for CA SDI, NJ TDI/FLI, NY PFL/DBL, WA PFML/Cares, CO FAMLI, OR, CT, DE or MN, whose annual caps are calendar-year accumulators of wages paid (the same payment-year basis as 58420). Selecting their Dec-2026-earned / Jan-2027-paid rate by date earned is an unsourced assumption (e.g. CA SDI 1.3% vs 1.4%).
findings.expected: 58428 applies to MA PFML only (ma.pfml.rate.selection_basis). Every other programme uses 58420 (payment date) until a registered source per programme says 'earned'. Raise a research request for the selection basis of each programme with a 2027 change (CA, CO, NJ, NY, WA).

_students_medicare_ruling: The builder is right. IRC 3121(b)(10) takes the student's service out of 'employment' for FICA as a whole, so both OASDI and Medicare are exempt (fed.students.treatment [US-FEDS5-029]). R1 finding QA1-14(a) reported that the r1 design charged students Medicare because 58411 did not gate 58512/58513; it never claimed students owe Medicare. With the gate in place the defect is closed.
